lines.L01: This morning’s control: {hookZ} SD above the mean.
lines.L02: Stop the run — or report the patients?
lines.L03: A Levey–Jennings chart plots every control result against its target mean and SD.
lines.L04: Targets come from your own control data: about twenty values to start.
lines.L05: Each result becomes a z-score: how many SDs it sits from the mean.
lines.L06: One value beyond 2 SD is the 1-2s rule: a warning, not a rejection.
lines.L07: Inspect it with the other rules first.
lines.L08: 1-3s and R-4s point to random error: reject the run.
lines.L09: 2-2s, 4-1s and 10x point to systematic error — a shift.
lines.L10: Here, four values in a row beyond 1 SD: 4-1s. Reject, and find the cause.
lines.L11: In LabGuide, enter each level’s target mean and SD — and where they came from.
lines.L12: Record every run; the app draws the Levey–Jennings chart.
lines.L13: Westgard rules are checked on every run, and the broken rule is named.
lines.L14: A rejected run stays in the history, but is not used in later rules or statistics.
lines.L15: Copy the runs as a table — data stays on this device.
lines.L16: A control result is a decision, not just a dot.

spoken._doc: TTS-only respellings (same words as the subtitle line). Subtitles always use `lines`.
spoken.L01: This morning’s control: two point three S D above the mean.
spoken.L03: A Levey Jennings chart plots every control result against its target mean and S D.
spoken.L05: Each result becomes a z score: how many S Ds it sits from the mean.
spoken.L06: One value beyond two S D is the one two s rule: a warning, not a rejection.
spoken.L08: One three s and R four s point to random error: reject the run.
spoken.L09: Two two s, four one s and ten x point to systematic error — a shift.
spoken.L10: Here, four values in a row beyond one S D: four one s. Reject, and find the cause.
spoken.L11: In Lab Guide, enter each level’s target mean and S D — and where they came from.
spoken.L12: Record every run; the app draws the Levey Jennings chart.
spoken.L13: Westgard rules are checked on every run, and the broken rule is named.
spoken.L17: Lab Guide: Lab, then Quality control.

ui.illustrative: Illustrative control data — not a real lot
ui.targetsNote: Targets: your lab’s control data (~20 values to start)
ui.d_R-4s: one above +2 SD, another below −2 SD, same run
ui.d_2-2s: two in a row beyond 2 SD, same side
ui.d_4-1s: four in a row beyond 1 SD, same side
ui.d_10x: ten in a row on one side of the mean
ui.computedRules: verdicts computed with the app’s rule engine

ui.ctaNote: A checking aid — it does not replace your laboratory’s QC procedure.
